recommendation: Keep the audit commit as-is. Do not restore the exact FHIR-23040 replacement phrase, because FHIR-49693 is the later approved wording for the same active source row.
issue_request: FHIR-23040 was a Published/Persuasive FHIR-I correction asking that ElementDefinition.binding.description stop saying "Human explanation of the value set" because the description explains the binding, not the value set. The requested R5 replacement was "Intended use of codes in the bound value set".
initial_application: The issue was applied in source history by commits 371c0b93c9 and de177bcf39, then merged by 86647c8abd in PR #1791. Those commits changed source/datatypes/elementdefinition.xml from "Human explanation of the value set" to "Intended use of codes in the bound value set".
additional_context: ElementDefinition is an active datatype in source/fhir.ini, so source/datatypes/elementdefinition.xml is current build-scope source. Later Applied/Persuasive issue FHIR-49693 revised the same row for R6 because bindings do not always have a concrete list of codes; commit d2eb91e8ff changed the current short text to "Guidance on the codes to be used", the definition to "Free-text guidance on the codes that are appropriate for this element.", and added a comment covering ad-hoc guidance, value-set context, and additional bindings.
reconciliation: Published an empty no-change audit commit. No source edit is needed because the old erroneous wording is absent and the current later-approved wording still describes code/binding guidance rather than a human explanation of the value set.
